title: Artificial intelligence meets genomic selection: comparing deep learning and GBLUP across diverse plant datasets
key_finding: Head-to-head comparison of tuned deep learning vs GBLUP on 14 real plant-breeding datasets: DL was often better, especially on smaller datasets, but neither method won consistently across traits and scenarios; DL success hinged on careful hyperparameter tuning.
wow_factor: An honest scoreboard: the 'deep learning revolution' in genomic selection is a draw that depends on the trait — a research gap students can attack.
suggested_slide: DL vs GBLUP: the honest scoreboard
verified_via: crossref DOI lookup + Europe PMC abstract

title: A review of multimodal deep learning methods for genomic-enabled prediction in plant breeding
key_finding: Review of multimodal DL (fusing genomic, environmental, phenomic and other inputs) for genomic prediction: multimodal DL improves on unimodal DL and other ML in many applications but demands more compute and careful choice of architecture and fusion strategy.
wow_factor: The future model doesn't read SNPs alone — it fuses genomes, drones, weather and omics like a self-driving car fuses sensors.
verified_via: crossref DOI lookup + Europe PMC abstract

title: Cropformer: An interpretable deep learning framework for crop genomic prediction
key_finding: Cropformer (CNN + multiple self-attention layers) was evaluated on >20 traits across maize, rice, wheat, foxtail millet and tomato, with up to 7.5% higher prediction accuracy than the runner-up model; attention weights were used to flag trait-associated SNPs.
wow_factor: Attention maps turn a black-box predictor into a gene-hunting tool — prediction and discovery in one model.
verified_via: crossref DOI lookup + Europe PMC abstract

title: Global genotype by environment prediction competition reveals that diverse modeling strategies can deliver satisfactory maize yield estimates
key_finding: Results of the first public Genomes to Fields GxE prediction competition (2022–2023, 9 years of maize data): the winner combined an environment-focused ML model (random forest, ridge, least squares features) with a genetics model; top teams used quantitative genetics, ML/DL, crop models and ensembles — no single strategy was far superior.
wow_factor: Some competitors had no plant-genetics training — open data lets anyone, including students, compete at the frontier.
verified_via: crossref DOI lookup + Europe PMC abstract; full text (PMC)

title: Genomes to fields 2024 maize genotype by environment prediction competition
key_finding: Data note for the G2F 2024 maize GxE competition (run Nov 15 2024–Jan 15 2025): training data from 2014–2023 covering ~180,000 field plots, 5,205 hybrids, 272 year-location environments and 2,425 SNPs, plus soil, weather and environmental covariates; winners ranked by average Pearson r.
wow_factor: One of the largest public plant G×E datasets ever released — ready for a student's laptop and a coding agent.
suggested_slide: Big open data: G2F by the numbers
verified_via: crossref DOI lookup + Europe PMC abstract; full text (PMC)

title: EXGEP: a framework for predicting genotype-by-environment interactions using ensembles of explainable machine-learning models
key_finding: EXGEP, an ensemble of explainable ML models, predicted maize grain yield from 70,693 records on 3,793 hybrids with genotype + environment data, beating Bayesian ridge regression by 17.37–42.35% across four data combinations; SHAP values exposed key G and E features and their interactions.
wow_factor: Explainable AI that tells breeders *which* weather window and *which* loci drive yield in each environment.
verified_via: crossref DOI lookup + Europe PMC abstract

title: Omics-driven plant breeding through phenomics-enviromics crosstalk
key_finding: Perspective proposing phenomics–enviromics 'crosstalk': synchronised, AI-assisted phenotyping (satellites, UAVs, ground vehicles, indoor facilities) and envirotyping to make genomic effects interpretable and predictable.
wow_factor: Satellites + drones + AI make every field a sensor-rich lab — the environment becomes as measurable as the genome.
verified_via: crossref DOI lookup + Europe PMC abstract

title: Phenotype prediction in plants is improved by integrating large-scale transcriptomic datasets
key_finding: ML models trained on highly variable genes from 21,612 public maize bulk RNA-seq samples accurately classified tissue, developmental stage, cultivar and stress condition; the approach generalised to rice within-species, but maize-trained models transferred poorly to rice.
wow_factor: Public transcriptome archives are a sleeping giant of training data for phenotype prediction.
verified_via: crossref DOI lookup + Europe PMC abstract

title: A foundational large language model for edible plant genomes
key_finding: AgroNT, a 1-billion-parameter DNA language model trained on genomes of 48 plant species (mostly crops), reached state-of-the-art on regulatory annotation, promoter/terminator strength, tissue-specific expression and variant prioritisation; >10 million cassava mutations were scored in silico, and the Plants Genomic Benchmark was released.
wow_factor: A 'ChatGPT for crop DNA' that is free on HuggingFace and pre-scored 10 million cassava mutations.
suggested_slide: AgroNT: an LLM for edible plant genomes
verified_via: crossref DOI lookup + Europe PMC abstract

title: Cross-species modeling of plant genomes at single-nucleotide resolution using a pretrained DNA language model
topic: Plant DNA language model / variant effect prediction
key_finding: PlantCaduceus, pre-trained on 16 angiosperm genomes, was fine-tuned on Arabidopsis labels and transferred to maize (160 My divergence), outperforming the best previous DNA LM 1.45-fold for splice-donor and 7.23-fold for translation-initiation prediction; its predicted deleterious mutations had 3-fold lower minor allele frequencies than MSA-based calls.
wow_factor: Train on Arabidopsis, predict in maize — 160 million years of evolution bridged by one model.
verified_via: crossref DOI lookup + Europe PMC abstract

title: PlantCAD2: A DNA foundation model for interpreting genomes across flowering plants
key_finding: PlantCAD2 (676M parameters, 65 angiosperm genomes, 8,192-bp context) beat the 7B-parameter Evo 2 in 10 of 12 zero-shot tasks and outperformed 1B-parameter AgroNT on seven cross-species tasks; maize accessible-chromatin AUPRC rose from 0.587 to 0.711 with longer context.
wow_factor: A plant-specialist model 10x smaller beats a 7-billion-parameter generalist — domain data beats brute scale.
verified_via: crossref DOI lookup + Europe PMC abstract

title: DNA language models are powerful predictors of genome-wide variant effects
topic: DNA language model variant effect prediction (plants)
key_finding: GPN, trained unsupervised on Arabidopsis thaliana and seven other Brassicales genomes, learned gene structure and DNA motifs without labels and predicted variant effects (validated with 1001 Genomes allele frequencies and GWAS) better than phyloP and phastCons conservation scores.
wow_factor: A model that learned genes and motifs by itself from raw plant DNA, no annotation needed.
suggested_slide: GPN: the plant DNA LM that started it
verified_via: crossref DOI lookup + Europe PMC abstract

title: A DNA language model based on multispecies alignment predicts the effects of genome-wide variants
topic: Alignment-aware DNA LM variant effect prediction
key_finding: GPN-MSA uses whole-genome multispecies alignments, trains in a few hours, and achieved top deleteriousness prediction for coding and non-coding human variants across ClinVar, COSMIC, OMIM, DMS, DepMap and gnomAD benchmarks; scores for ~9 billion possible SNVs were released.
wow_factor: Score every possible mutation in a genome in advance — the same blueprint could pre-score every SNP in a crop pan-genome.
verified_via: crossref DOI lookup + Europe PMC abstract

title: Sequence modeling and design from molecular to genome scale with Evo
key_finding: Evo, a long-context genomic foundation model trained on millions of prokaryotic and phage genomes, reported DNA scaling laws, zero-shot function prediction across DNA/RNA/protein, and generated functional CRISPR-Cas and transposon systems plus megabase-scale sequences.
wow_factor: The first language model to design working CRISPR systems — biology became writable, not just readable.
verified_via: crossref DOI lookup + Europe PMC abstract

title: Genome modeling and design across all domains of life with Evo 2
topic: Genomic foundation model across all domains of life
key_finding: Evo 2 (7B and 40B parameters) was trained on 9.3 trillion DNA base pairs from all domains of life with a 1-million-token context, predicts variant effects without task-specific fine-tuning, and generates genome-scale sequences; weights, code and the OpenGenome2 dataset are fully open.
wow_factor: A 1-million-base context window means a model can 'see' an entire gene neighbourhood — including plant regulatory landscapes — at once.
suggested_slide: Evo 2: one model for all life
verified_via: crossref DOI lookup + Europe PMC abstract

title: Generative design of bacteriophages with genome language models
key_finding: Genome language models generated complete bacteriophage genomes based on ΦX174; experimental testing yielded 16 viable phages, and a cocktail of generated phages overcame ΦX174-resistant E. coli strains.
wow_factor: AI has written whole working genomes — a glimpse of what 'designed' crop regulatory sequences might look like.
verified_via: crossref DOI lookup + Europe PMC abstract

title: Evo 2’s perception of single nucleotide substitutions in the genes of two plant model organisms
key_finding: Evo 2 assigned, on average, lower likelihood (higher perplexity) to simulated single-nucleotide substitutions than to substitutions observed in vivo in Arabidopsis and rice genes — statistically robust but modest in effect size.
wow_factor: Even generalist models 'sense' plant evolutionary constraint — but the honest effect is small, leaving room for plant-specific models.
verified_via: crossref DOI lookup + Europe PMC abstract; Open Research Europe v1 (post-publication peer review status not confirmed)

title: An interpretable RNA foundation model for exploring functional RNA motifs in plants
key_finding: PlantRNA-FM, pre-trained on RNA sequences and structures from 1,124 plant species, reached F1 = 0.974 for genic-region annotation vs 0.639 for the previous best model, and its interpretable framework revealed translation-associated RNA motifs that were validated experimentally.
wow_factor: 1,124 species in one model and an F1 jump from 0.64 to 0.97 — and the motifs it found were confirmed in the lab.
suggested_slide: PlantRNA-FM: the RNA language of plants
verified_via: crossref DOI lookup + Europe PMC abstract

title: Deep learning the cis-regulatory code for gene expression in selected model plants
key_finding: Interpretable CNNs predicted gene expression from gene-flanking sequences in Arabidopsis, tomato, sorghum and maize with >80% accuracy, transferred across species, linked genetic variation to expression changes across 14 tomato genomes, and highlighted the role of UTRs.
wow_factor: Read a promoter, predict expression — and explain why a wild drought-tolerant tomato behaves differently.
verified_via: crossref DOI lookup + Europe PMC abstract

title: DeepCBA: A deep learning framework for gene expression prediction in maize based on DNA sequences and chromatin interactions
key_finding: DeepCBA predicted maize gene expression from DNA sequence plus chromatin-interaction data with an average PCC of 0.929 using proximal + distal interactions, 0.469 higher than methods using proximal sequence only; promoter editing of ZmCLE7 and ZmVTE4 validated its use for designing expression.
wow_factor: From prediction to editing: the model's suggested promoter changes were tested by genome editing in maize.
verified_via: crossref DOI lookup + Europe PMC abstract

title: Evolutionary and Deep Learning Models Highlight Deleterious Mutations Behind the History of Sugar Beet Breeding
topic: Variant effect prediction in a crop
key_finding: PlantCaduceus combined with PAML and PhyloP defined ~5k high-confidence deleterious variants, scored across >1,900 sequenced wild and cultivated beets; domesticated beets carried higher load than wild maritima, and load declined over a century of US sugar beet entries.
wow_factor: A DNA language model reads a century of breeding history — and points to mutations to purge next.
suggested_slide: Purging genetic load with DNA LMs
verified_via: crossref DOI lookup + Europe PMC abstract

title: OneGenome-Rice (OGR): A genomic foundation model for rice
key_finding: OneGenome-Rice: a 1.25B-parameter mixture-of-experts model pre-trained on 422 cultivated and wild rice genomes with up to 1 Mb context; reported to outperform multi-plant and all-life models in 11 benchmark categories and applied to introgression analysis, trait-locus identification and expression prediction.
wow_factor: A pan-genome-scale foundation model for a single staple crop — the 'rice GPT' era has started.
verified_via: crossref DOI lookup + Europe PMC abstract

title: Integrating pan-genome analysis, GWAS, and interpretable machine learning to prioritize trait-associated structural variations in Setaria italica
key_finding: Eight new reference-quality foxtail millet assemblies formed a graph pan-genome; GWAS on 344 accessions plus interpretable ML prioritised large-effect structural variants for leaf-colour traits, including a 5,002-bp Copia insertion on chromosome 7.
wow_factor: Pan-genomes reveal the hidden structural variants that SNP chips miss — and ML pinpoints the causal ones.
verified_via: crossref DOI lookup + Europe PMC abstract

title: scPlantLLM: A Foundation Model for Exploring Single-cell Expression Atlases in Plants
key_finding: scPlantLLM, a transformer pre-trained on millions of plant single-cell profiles, achieved up to 0.91 zero-shot cell-type annotation accuracy in Arabidopsis and outperformed traditional methods on ARI, NMI and silhouette clustering metrics, also inferring gene regulatory networks.
wow_factor: Cell-type annotation without labels — a foundation model that knows plant cells.
verified_via: crossref DOI lookup + Europe PMC abstract

title: scMaize: A Single-Cell Foundation Model and Integrated Atlas for Maize
key_finding: scMaize integrates 385,675 maize cells from 20 projects and 7 tissues; its GO-informed model reached 86.0% cell-type and 97.1% tissue classification accuracy, generalised zero-shot across species and amplified perturbation signals ~3-fold.
wow_factor: A crop-specific cell atlas plus foundation model with a zero-code web platform — single-cell AI for breeders.
suggested_slide: scMaize: a cell atlas for a crop
verified_via: crossref DOI lookup + Europe PMC abstract
